scenarios.title: The Letter From a Kid
scenarios.text: A letter arrives at the facility from a kid you met in a hospital years ago. He's twelve now, and walking, and he's enclosed a photo of himself standing next to a football.

choices.label: Write back
choices.result: A handwritten reply, two pages, with a signed photo of your own. He frames it, and his mother sends you a picture of it on his wall.

choices.label: Invite him to a practice
choices.result: An invitation to practice, for him and his family. He walks onto the field himself, slowly, and the whole team stops to clap.

choices.label: Keep the letter
choices.result: The letter goes in your locker, next to your cleats. On bad days you read it again, and it fixes something every time.

choices.label: Go back to the hospital
choices.result: You go back to the hospital where you met him, and you bring his letter to show the kids there.

scenarios.title: The Awards Show
scenarios.text: The league's awards show wants you on the red carpet the night before a practice you can't miss. There's a tuxedo waiting at your hotel and a car at seven.

choices.label: Walk the carpet and leave early
choices.result: The carpet, two interviews and gone before dessert. You make practice on time the next morning, tired and secretly pleased.

choices.label: Ask {coach}
choices.result: {coach} says go, and be on time. You are, at six in the morning, with makeup still behind your ear.

choices.label: Watch from home
choices.result: The awards, watched from home in sweatpants. You cheer loudly for the punter who wins, and you're asleep by ten.

scenarios.title: Thirty
scenarios.text: You turn thirty in camp, and the trainer starts using the word 'maintenance' in every conversation. Your birthday cake has a candle shaped like an ice pack.

choices.label: Listen to the trainer
choices.result: The new maintenance routine, added without complaint: bands, heat, an extra stretching block. It's dull and it works, and your hip stops talking to you in the mornings.

choices.label: Prove you don't need it
choices.result: No maintenance, thanks; you'll prove you don't need it. Your body disagrees by October, loudly, and the trainer says nothing, which is worse.

choices.label: Celebrate with the unit
choices.result: A birthday in the cafeteria, thrown by the specialists, with the ice-pack candle and a terrible song. {holder} gives a speech about your age.

scenarios.title: The Maintenance Bill
scenarios.text: Holding on to your leg costs more every year: more treatment, more rest days, more hours in the cold tub, and more of the life outside the facility.

choices.label: Plan the year around recovery
choices.result: The whole year, planned around recovery like a second job. It's tedious, and your leg is the best it's been in three seasons.

choices.label: Work harder instead
choices.result: Harder, not smarter: more reps, more lifting, more hours. It holds, for now, and you can feel the bill coming for next year.

choices.label: Rest more, train less
choices.result: More rest, less training. Your leg feels fresh on game days and a little slower in practice, and you can't decide if that's wisdom.

scenarios.title: The Anniversary
scenarios.text: Another wedding anniversary, and you're in a hotel room in a city you can't remember the name of, with a road game tomorrow. {love_interest} is home with the dog and a cake.

choices.label: Fly {love_interest} in
choices.result: A ticket for the last flight in, booked from the team bus. One night together in a strange city, and it's the best anniversary yet.

choices.label: Plan the real celebration
choices.result: The real celebration, planned for the bye week, down to the restaurant and the song. You talk about it all night on the phone.

choices.label: Call for an hour
choices.result: An hour on the phone from the hotel, talking about the first year: the tiny apartment, the bad car. It's enough, almost.

scenarios.title: {sibling}'s Family
scenarios.text: {sibling} has kids of his own now, two of them, and they think you're the most famous person alive. They have your jersey, your card and a poster above the bunk bed.

choices.label: Be the fun uncle for a day
choices.result: A whole day with them: the zoo, the park, ice cream twice. They tell their entire school about it for a year, and {sibling} looks at you differently.

choices.label: Teach them to kick
choices.result: Kicking lessons in {sibling}'s backyard, with a net and a lot of patience. The younger one is actually good, which {sibling} finds hilarious.

choices.label: Send signed gear
choices.result: Signed gear and a video message, mailed with a long note. They wear the jerseys to bed for a month.

scenarios.title: The Radio Show
scenarios.text: A local radio station offers you a weekly show during the season: an hour on Wednesday nights, your name in the title, and callers who want to talk about everything but kicking.

choices.label: Say yes
choices.result: Yes, every Wednesday. The callers love you, a few teammates call in under fake names, and you become the voice of the club for a season.

choices.label: Do it in the offseason
choices.result: An offseason show only, you counter, and they agree. It's relaxed and fun, and you never have to talk about a loss the night after.

choices.label: Keep your Wednesdays
choices.result: No show this year. Your Wednesday nights stay quiet and yours, and the station hires a retired linebacker who shouts a lot.

scenarios.title: A Franchise Offer
scenarios.text: A restaurant chain offers you a franchise with your name on it: real professionals running it this time, a real contract, and your face on the menu.

choices.label: Do it with professionals
choices.result: Signed, with professionals running it and two lawyers reading everything first. It opens in March, and the burger named after you is surprisingly good.

choices.label: Bring family in
choices.result: {sibling}, brought in to keep an eye on things for you. It's a family project now, and {sibling} turns out to be good at it.

choices.label: Stay out of restaurants
choices.result: No franchise for you. You have enough to think about already, and you've watched what restaurants did to two teammates' savings accounts.

scenarios.title: The Comeback Year
scenarios.text: Last year everyone wrote your obituary: released, or benched, and called finished in print. This year you're the first one on the field every single morning.

choices.label: Be first every day
choices.result: First on the field and last off it, every day. By September nobody is writing obituaries, and the columnist who wrote the worst one apologizes.

choices.label: Bring the young players
choices.result: The young players, invited to your early sessions. It becomes a club, and the club becomes the core of the team.

choices.label: Prove it with numbers
choices.result: Every kick, charted, and the curve left on {coach}'s desk every Friday. The numbers do all the arguing for you, quietly.

scenarios.title: Who Am I Without It
scenarios.text: A sleepless night at three in the morning, the question you've been avoiding finally sitting on your chest: if you're not the kicker, who are you?

choices.label: Wake {love_interest}
choices.result: {love_interest}, woken gently, and you talk until dawn. By morning you have half an answer and a much fuller heart.

choices.label: Write it all down
choices.result: Everything you are besides a kicker, written on a legal pad. The list is longer than you thought, and some of it surprises you.

choices.label: Walk until it's light
choices.result: A walk at three in the morning, through an empty neighborhood. The question comes with you, and so does the sunrise.

scenarios.title: The Camp You Teach
scenarios.text: A youth camp asks you to coach for a week in July. The kids kick terribly, fall over constantly, and have more fun than you've had in years.

choices.label: Coach every station
choices.result: Every station, coached by you, all week. By Friday three of them can actually kick, and one of them cries when his first one clears the bar.

choices.label: Play with them as much as coach
choices.result: Half coaching, half playing: tag, relay races, a kicking contest you lose on purpose. You laugh all week and go home sunburned and happy.

choices.label: Coach the mornings only
choices.result: The mornings, coached properly, and the afternoons for rest. It's a good balance, and the head counselor is grateful for any of it.

scenarios.title: The Family Vacation
scenarios.text: A real family vacation, a whole week, no phones, and a family that's not used to having you around for seven straight days. The kids keep asking when you're leaving.

choices.label: Be completely there
choices.result: The phone, in a drawer, all week. You build sandcastles, lose at board games and fall asleep on the beach, and everyone notices.

choices.label: Plan every day
choices.result: Every day planned: the boat, the museum, the hike. It's fun and a little exhausting, and the kids love the boat.

choices.label: Train every morning
choices.result: Every morning, a run and a kicking session before anyone wakes up. You're there for the rest, mostly, and {love_interest} notices the mornings.

scenarios.title: Back to Your College
scenarios.text: Your college invites you back for spring practice. The kicking net is in the same place, the equipment manager is the same man, and the cafeteria still serves the same terrible pasta.

choices.label: Coach their kickers for a day
choices.result: Their kickers, coached by you for a whole day. They follow you everywhere, ask a hundred questions and kick better by the end.

choices.label: Find the old staff
choices.result: The equipment manager, the trainers, the woman who ran the cafeteria. They tell stories about you that you'd rather forget, and you love every one.

choices.label: Stand by the net for a while
choices.result: The facility, walked alone, and a long time standing by the old net. You think about the kid who kicked there, and how far he came.
